intro: Studies find that apologies, empathy, and perceived sincerity go with more forgiveness, and that forgiveness and self-forgiveness programs can help the person doing the work. Evidence that any of this repairs a particular relationship is limited, and forgiveness is the other person's to give.

items.title: The Road to Forgiveness: A Meta-Analytic Synthesis of Its Situational and Dispositional Correlates
items.publisher: Psychological Bulletin (Fehr, Gelfand, and Nag, 2010), hosted by the Greater Good Science Center
items.finding: Across 175 studies, receiving an apology was associated with more forgiveness (average r = .42), alongside the offender's intent, empathy, and anger.

items.title: Restorative Justice Conferencing (RJC) Using Face-to-Face Meetings of Offenders and Victims: Effects on Offender Recidivism and Victim Satisfaction
items.publisher: Campbell Systematic Reviews 2013:12 (copy hosted by the Alaska Judicial Council)
items.finding: In the Canberra experiment, 72 percent of victims assigned to a conference said they received an apology, compared with 19 percent of those whose cases went to court.

items.title: Forgiving the self and physical and mental health correlates: A meta-analytic review
items.publisher: Journal of Counseling Psychology (Davis and colleagues, 2015)
items.finding: Self-forgiveness correlated with psychological well-being (r = .45, 65 samples) and physical health (r = .32, 18 samples), but these are correlations that do not show cause.

items.title: Psychological interventions to promote self-forgiveness: a systematic review
items.finding: In 21 articles that varied widely in design, self-directed interventions, notably those based on Enright's process model, appeared to help build self-forgiveness.

items.title: Forgiveness Therapy For The Promotion of Mental Wellbeing: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
items.publisher: Oxford University Research Archive (Akhtar and Barlow)
items.finding: Forgiveness therapy trials were associated with less depression and distress and more positive emotion, though the authors say more research is needed on how well it compares with other treatments.

items.title: The Liverpool Desistance Study and probation practice: Opening the dialogue
items.finding: The authors report that themes of redemption and overcoming challenges were especially salient among people who had stopped offending, while stressing the study was not designed to test what works.

items.title: Reconciling 'Desistance' and 'What Works'
items.publisher: HM Inspectorate of Probation, Academic Insights (Maruna and Mann, 2019)
items.finding: Maruna and Mann treat desistance research and program evaluation as two kinds of evidence that share a belief that people can change.

limits: Most apology and forgiveness findings are correlations, often from students imagining or recalling hurts, and desistance research is largely interview-based with small samples. These sheets do not claim that apologizing or repaying a debt will win anyone's forgiveness or trust back.
